questions.text: Provide a brief description of your business or, organisation including any relationships with IAG, RAC and/or RACI.
Outline any concerns you have regarding the impact of the Acquisition on competition.

questions.section: Questions about IAG’s public benefit submissions
questions.text: Provide any views you have on the extent and likelihood of IAG’s claimed public benefits arising from the Acquisition.

bullets: reinsurance synergies through IAG’s scale, geographic diversification and established relationships with reinsurers
claims cost synergies resulting from IAG’s technical and support functions, including with respect to fraud detection, claims management capability

expense synergies, including from the consolidation of duplicated corporate and technology functions. Provide a view on whether the above synergies would flow through to RACI and IAG policyholders and/or RAC members and IAG shareholders
questions.section: Questions about IAG’s public benefit submissions
questions.text: Provide any views you have on the extent and likelihood that the Acquisition would lead to:

questions.section: Questions about IAG’s public benefit submissions
questions.text: Provide any views you have on the extent and likelihood that the Acquisition would benefit RACI policyholders and the broader Australian public by enhancing the financial resilience of RACI, and reduce the risk of RACI requiring government intervention and public resources in response to a major peril event.

questions.section: Questions about IAG’s public benefit submissions
questions.text: Provide any views you have you have on the extent and likelihood that the Acquisition would benefit RAC members and the broader WA community by increasing RAC’s ability to invest in and expand its community initiatives.

questions.section: Questions about IAG’s public benefit submissions
questions.text: Provide any views you have on the extent and likelihood that the Acquisition would result in any other public benefits, including IAG’s proposal for RACI insurance products, to be underwritten by IAG, to be available in Northern Western Australia (above the 26th parallel).

questions.section: Questions about public benefit remedy offer
questions.text: Describe the extent to which the divestiture obligations in Part A of the undertaking (including Schedule 5), requiring IAG to divest IAG’s “renewal rights” in respect of its NRMA home and contents and motor insurance book in WA and, at the option of the purchaser, the SGIO brand would address competition detriments associated with the Acquisition and/or provide public benefits.

questions.section: Questions about public benefit remedy offer
questions.text: Describe the extent to which the behavioural obligations in Part B (clauses 10-14 inclusive) of the undertaking would address competition detriments associated with the Acquisition and/or provide public benefits.

questions.section: Questions about public benefit remedy offer
questions.text: Provide any additional information or comments you consider relevant to the ACCC’s consideration of the remedy offer.

Provide a brief description of your business or, organisation including any relationships with IAG, RAC and/or RACI.
Outline any concerns you have regarding the impact of the Acquisition on competition.

questions.section: Questions about motor insurance and home and contents insurance
questions.text: Explain whether there are any features of the motor insurance and/or home and contents insurance markets in Western Australia and/or certain areas of Western Australia which differ compared to the rest of Australia.

questions.section: Questions about motor insurance and home and contents insurance
questions.text: Describe how effective a competitor RACI is in Western Australia, and on what factors it competes most strongly (e.g. price, service quality, coverage, etc). Also explain on what factors it does not compete strongly.

questions.section: Questions about motor insurance and home and contents insurance
questions.text: Describe how effective a competitor IAG is in Western Australia, and on what factors it competes most strongly (e.g. price, service quality, coverage, etc). Also explain on what factors it does not compete strongly.

questions.section: Questions about motor insurance and home and contents insurance
questions.text: Describe how closely IAG and RACI compete in the supply of motor insurance and/or home and contents insurance Western Australia (e.g. in terms of price, service quality, coverage, etc).

questions.section: Questions about motor insurance and home and contents insurance
questions.text: Explain how strongly established insurers and mid-tier insurers compete in Western Australia. Explain the extent to which established insurer and mid- tier insurers would prevent the merged IAG/RACI from increasing premiums, reducing coverage, reducing its product range or diminishing the service provided in Western Australia. Please also include the level of constraint insurers with larger market shares outside of Western Australia are likely to impose.

questions.section: Questions about motor insurance and home and contents insurance
questions.text: Explain any challenges being faced by the insurance industry and the impact this could have on insurers and insurance products, including whether RACI is likely to experience heightened vulnerability to these challenges as a state- based, mutual organisation.

questions.section: Questions about motor insurance and home and contents insurance
questions.text: Identify any insurers that have entered or exited in the last 12 months or known upcoming examples of entry or exit in the supply of motor and home and contents insurance in Western Australia or Australia.

questions.section: Questions about repair services
questions.text: Explain the extent to which the merged IAG/RACI would be in an enhanced position to foreclose or frustrate competing insurers' access to each of (i) smash repair services, (ii) windscreen repair and replacement services, and (iii) building repair services.

questions.section: Questions about repair services
questions.text: Explain the extent to which the merged entity IAG/RACI would be able to reduce prices or degrade the terms on which it acquires repair services. Please explain why you consider the merged entity would (or would not) be able to do this, including whether competition from other insurers would prevent the merged entity from doing so.

questions.section: Other issues
questions.text: Provide any additional information or comments that you consider relevant to the ACCC’s assessment of the Acquisition.
